To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV-specific CD8 T cell immunity is rapidly induced in primary HIV infection and that the breadth and magnitude of this immune response is directly correlated to the duration of infection.
HIV-specific effector CD8+ T cell activity can be detected in patients within 1 week of infection and that the magnitude and breadth increase during the first year after infection.
HIV-specific CD8 T cells are detectable during the first year after infection, and their magnitude and breadth increase during the first 2 months of HIV infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the HIV-specific effector CD8+ T cell response in patients during primary HIV infection.
the role of CD8+ T cells in the immune response to human immunodeficiency viruses (HIVs).
understanding the mechanisms of HIV pathogenesis, with the ultimate goal of developing effective therapeutic strategies.

HIV-specific CD8 T cells were detectable in the blood during the early phase of infection, but their magnitude and breadth were significantly lower than in subjects with chronic infection.
the magnitude and breadth (number of different epitope responses) of HIV-specific CD8 T cell effector responses in primary HIV infection are greater than those seen in chronic infection.
the magnitude and breadth (number of epitopes recognized) of HIV-specific effectors T cell responses in the first year of infection is significantly higher than in chronic infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are two major findings: First, the magnitude of the response to the HIV peptides was greater during the acute phase of HIV infection compared to the chronic phase.
the breadth and magnitude of HIV peptide-specific responses are significantly greater during the acute phase of infection compared to the chronic phase.

the HIV-specific effector CD8 response is a dynamic phenomenon that evolves during the first year postinfection and that maximal magnitude and breadth are achieved within the first 2-4 months after exposure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a very rapid expansion of HIV-specific CD8 T cell immunity that occurs during the primary phase of HIV infection.
the magnitude and breadth (number of epitopes recognized) of the HIV-specific CD8 T cell response increases with time after exposure.

HIV-specific CD8 T cell effector function can be detected in most subjects within the first year after exposure to HIV, and the magnitude of this response is significantly correlated with the time elapsed from exposure.
